why: Following a jacket zipper's tape, teeth, slider, pin and stops helps your child explain how small parts work together to fasten something.
teaser: Meet the tape, teeth and slider, then find the hidden lock, the pin and the stops.
title: How a Zipper Holds Shut and Comes Apart
question: What holds a zipper shut, and what lets a jacket zipper come all the way apart?
idea: A zipper is two cloth tapes with rows of teeth; the slider meshes or parts the teeth, a lock keeps it still, a pin and box start a jacket, and stops keep the slider on.

curiosity.intro: Start with one jacket zipper. Find its parts, how the teeth hold, and what each small piece at the ends is for.
curiosity.carryForward: Look for the tape, the teeth, the slider, and the little pieces at each end.

questions.question: What are the main parts of a zipper?
questions.notice: Find the two cloth strips, the rows of small teeth on them, and the one slider that rides along the teeth.
questions.say: A zipper has three main parts. The tape is the cloth strip sewn to the jacket. The teeth, also called elements, are fixed in a row along each tape. The slider is the piece you pull up and down to join or part the teeth.
questions.try: Find a zipper on a jacket, bag or pencil case. Point to the tape, the teeth and the slider, and say each name out loud.

questions.question: How do the teeth hold the two sides together?
questions.notice: Compare the open teeth at the bottom with the joined teeth at the top. See how each tooth sits between two teeth on the other side.
questions.say: Each tooth has a little bump on one side and a hollow on the other. The teeth on the left are set halfway between the teeth on the right. When the slider presses them together, each bump tucks into the hollow of the next tooth, and a joined row of teeth is called the chain.
questions.try: Hold your hands flat with fingers spread. Slide them together so each finger fits between two fingers of the other hand. Now pull your hands apart sideways and feel how the fingers hold.

questions.question: Why doesn't a zipper slide open on its own?
questions.notice: Look at the pull-tab lying flat against the slider, and the tiny bump under the slider that sits between two teeth.
questions.say: Many sliders have a lock. When the pull-tab is let go or pressed flat, a tiny piece under the slider slips between the teeth and holds it still. Lifting the pull-tab moves that piece out of the way so the slider can move again.
questions.try: Find a zipper with a pull-tab. Let go of the tab and gently tug the two sides of the cloth. Then lift the tab and slide it. Tell what changed.

questions.question: How does a jacket zipper come all the way apart and start again?
questions.notice: Find the thin pin at the bottom of one tape and the little box at the bottom of the other tape, where the slider waits.
questions.say: A jacket zipper is an open-end zipper. One tape ends in a thin insert pin. The other tape ends in a retainer box that holds the slider at the bottom. Pushing the pin fully into the box lines the two rows up, so the slider can start meshing teeth from the very first pair.
questions.try: Look at the bottom of a jacket zipper. Find the pin and the box. Watch how the pin goes all the way in before the slider moves up.

beats.title: A jacket zipper
beats.passage: Big and Little found a jacket hanging on a peg, its zipper half closed. Above the slider the two sides were joined in one neat row. Below it they hung apart. Little wondered how one small piece could close a whole jacket. Big said a zipper is a team of small parts, each with its own job.
beats.prompt: Where on the zipper are the two sides joined, and where are they apart?

foldable.heading: A jacket zipper
foldable.body: Above the slider the two sides of a zipper are joined. Below it they hang apart. Each small part has its own job.

beats.title: Tape, teeth, slider
beats.passage: Laid flat on a table, a zipper shows its three main parts. The tape is the cloth strip that gets sewn to the jacket. The teeth, also called elements, are fixed in a row along each tape. The slider rides along both rows. Pull it one way and it joins the teeth. Pull it the other way and it parts them.
beats.prompt: Which part moves, and which parts stay in place on the cloth?

foldable.heading: Tape, teeth, slider
foldable.body: A zipper has three main parts: the cloth tape, the rows of teeth fixed on it, and the slider that joins or parts the teeth.

beats.title: Teeth that mesh
beats.passage: Up close, each tooth has a little bump on one side and a hollow on the other. The left teeth sit halfway between the right teeth, like fingers ready to fold together. Inside the slider, the two rows are squeezed together at an angle, so each bump tucks into the hollow of the next tooth. Teeth that fit together like this mesh, and the joined row is called the chain.
beats.prompt: Why must the teeth on one side sit halfway between the teeth on the other side?

foldable.heading: Teeth that mesh
foldable.body: Each tooth has a bump and a hollow. The slider squeezes the rows together, so each bump tucks into the next hollow.

beats.title: A hidden lock
beats.passage: Little tugged the two sides of the jacket, but the slider did not move. Big pointed under the slider. Many sliders hide a lock. When the pull-tab lies flat or is let go, a tiny piece slips between two teeth and holds the slider still. Lift the pull-tab and the piece moves out of the way, so the slider can glide again.
beats.prompt: What does lifting the pull-tab change inside the slider?

foldable.heading: A hidden lock
foldable.body: When the pull-tab lies flat, a tiny piece slips between two teeth and holds the slider still. Lifting the tab frees it.

beats.title: Pin into box
beats.passage: A jacket zipper comes all the way apart. It is called an open-end zipper. At the bottom, one tape ends in a thin insert pin, and the other ends in a small retainer box where the slider waits. The pin must go fully into the box. Then both rows start lined up, and the slider can mesh the very first pair of teeth.
beats.prompt: What could go wrong if the pin is only pushed halfway into the box?

foldable.heading: Pin into box
foldable.body: A jacket zipper comes apart. Its thin pin goes fully into a small box, so both rows start lined up for the slider.

beats.title: Stops at the ends
beats.passage: At the very top of the zipper, Little found a tiny metal piece above the last teeth. It is a top stop. A stop at each end keeps the slider from running off the teeth. On a jacket, the retainer box is the stop at the bottom. Tape, teeth, slider, lock, pin, box and stops all work together each time a jacket closes.
beats.prompt: Why does a zipper need a stop at each end of the teeth?

foldable.heading: Stops at the ends
foldable.body: A stop at each end keeps the slider from running off the teeth. On a jacket, the box is the stop at the bottom.

answers.label: Reading · 1
answers.text: The tape is the cloth strip sewn to the jacket, the teeth (elements) sit in a row on each tape, and the slider moves to join or part the teeth.

answers.label: Reading · 2
answers.text: Each tooth has a bump and a hollow, and the rows are offset, so the slider squeezes each bump into the next hollow. A lock under the slider slips between the teeth when the pull-tab is flat, so it stays still.

answers.label: Reading · 3
answers.text: A pin pushed fully into the box lines both rows up so the first teeth can mesh; if it is only halfway in, the rows start uneven. Stops at each end keep the slider from running off the teeth.

answers.label: Writing
answers.text: Accept a spoken, dictated, drawn, or written sentence that tells how one zipper part does its job.

parentGuidance: A zipper has three main parts: the tape, the elements (teeth) and the slider. Teeth on the two tapes are offset; inside the slider the rows are pressed together at an angle so each tooth's bump seats in the next tooth's hollow, forming the chain. Many sliders are automatic-lock: when the pull-tab is released, a small pin or claw under the slider drops between the teeth. Jacket zippers are open-end zippers: the insert pin must go fully into the retainer box before the slider is pulled up, or the rows start unevenly and the zipper may split or jam. Top and bottom stops keep the slider on the chain. Safety: keep fingers and loose skin clear of the slider and teeth; never zip near hair or skin, and keep small loose zipper parts away from young children.
